course.name: A2 Grammar: Everyday Accuracy with Nguyen Minh Ha

topicDescription: Describe completed events using regular and common irregular past forms.

lessons.title: Past Time and Regular Verb Endings
lessons.objective: Recognize completed past events and form regular past simple verbs with -ed.
lessons.description: Connect finished-time expressions to regular past forms.
lessons.content: Use the past simple for completed events at a finished time. Most regular verbs add -ed: visit becomes visited. Verbs ending in e add -d: live becomes lived. Verbs ending in consonant plus y change y to i and add -ed: study becomes studied.
commonErrors: Do not use the base form with a finished past-time expression: I watched a film yesterday.
For consonant plus y, change y to i before -ed: carry becomes carried.
lessons.guidedPractice: Find the finished-time expression, then change the regular verb to its past form.
lessons.summary: Use past simple for finished past events; most regular verbs take -ed with a few predictable spelling changes.

questions.questionText: We ___ our grandparents last Sunday.
questions.explanation: Last Sunday is a finished past time, so visit takes -ed.

questions.questionText: Maya ___ in a small town when she was a child.
questions.explanation: Live ends in e, so add -d to form lived.
questions.knowledgePoint: regular past verbs ending in e

questions.questionText: My brother ___ for the test yesterday evening.
questions.explanation: Study ends in consonant plus y, so change y to i and add -ed.

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes a completed event yesterday?
questions.explanation: Yesterday is finished time and cleaned is the past form of clean.

options.text: They are cleaning the kitchen yesterday.

questions.questionText: Last night, I ___ an email to my teacher.
questions.explanation: Answer is a regular verb; add -ed for a completed event last night.
questions.knowledgePoint: regular past in a finished-time sentence

questions.questionText: The children ___ their bags before the trip yesterday.
questions.explanation: Pack ends in a short vowel plus consonant, so double the final consonant before -ed.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct past form of stop.
questions.explanation: Stop has a short vowel followed by one final consonant, so double p before -ed.

questions.questionText: At the weekend, Lan ___ her room and helped her mother.
questions.explanation: Tidy ends in consonant plus y, so change y to i and add -ed.

questions.questionText: Which verb is already in the past simple?
questions.explanation: Watched is the regular past form of watch.

questions.questionText: Tom ___ the bus to work two days ago.
questions.explanation: Two days ago is finished past time; miss doubles s before -ed.

lessons.title: Common Irregular Verbs in Everyday Events
lessons.objective: Use common irregular past forms for familiar completed events.
lessons.description: Notice and practise frequent irregular verbs in short personal contexts.
lessons.content: Some frequent verbs do not take -ed in the past. Learn common pairs such as go/went, have/had, see/saw, buy/bought, take/took, eat/ate, make/made, and come/came. Use the past form for the completed event; the form does not change with he, she, or they.
examples: I went to the market yesterday.
They saw a new film last week.
commonErrors: Do not add -ed to an irregular past form: went, not goed.
Do not add present-tense -s to an irregular past verb: he went, not he goes yesterday.
lessons.guidedPractice: Match each base verb to its past form, then use it in a sentence with a finished-time expression.
lessons.summary: Common irregular verbs have special past forms that must be learned and used for all subjects.

questions.questionText: We ___ to the beach during our holiday last month.
questions.explanation: The past form of go is went.

questions.questionText: Ravi ___ lunch at a cafe yesterday.
questions.explanation: The past form of have is had.

questions.questionText: I ___ my old teacher at the station last night.
questions.explanation: The past form of see is saw.

questions.questionText: They ___ a new table for their kitchen last weekend.
questions.explanation: The past form of buy is bought.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correct?
questions.correctAnswer: He took a taxi to the airport yesterday.
questions.explanation: Take changes to took in the past simple and does not take -s.

options.text: He took a taxi to the airport yesterday.
He taked a taxi to the airport yesterday.

questions.questionText: My cousins ___ noodles at our house on Sunday.
questions.explanation: The past form of eat is ate.

questions.questionText: Nora ___ a birthday card for her friend yesterday.
questions.explanation: The past form of make is made.

questions.questionText: Our guests ___ home after dinner last night.
questions.explanation: The past form of come is came.

questions.questionText: Yesterday, I ___ my friend a message about the meeting.
questions.explanation: The past form of send is sent.

questions.questionText: The students ___ the answer after the teacher explained the problem.
questions.explanation: The past form of know is knew.

lessons.title: Past Simple Negatives and Questions with Did
lessons.objective: Form past simple negatives and yes/no or wh- questions with did and the base verb.
lessons.description: Practise do-support in questions and negative sentences about completed events.
lessons.content: Use did not (didn't) plus the base verb for a negative: She didn't call. Use did plus subject plus base verb for a yes/no question: Did you call? Use a wh-word before did: Where did they stay? The past meaning is carried by did, so the main verb stays in its base form.
examples: I didn't watch television last night.
Where did you put the tickets?
commonErrors: After did or didn't, use the base verb: didn't go, not didn't went.
In questions, put did before the subject: Did he arrive?
lessons.guidedPractice: Underline did/didn't, then check that the main verb is in its base form.
lessons.summary: Use did/didn't for past questions and negatives; keep the main verb in its base form.

questions.questionText: We ___ the match because it rained all afternoon.
questions.explanation: Use didn't plus the base verb play for a past negative.

questions.questionText: ___ Sara call you after the class yesterday?
questions.explanation: Use Did before the subject to form a past simple yes/no question.

questions.questionText: Where did your family ___ during the trip?
questions.explanation: After did, use the base form stay.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct negative sentence.
questions.explanation: Didn't is followed by the base verb bring.

questions.questionText: ___ they see the sign at the entrance?
questions.explanation: Use Did to form a past simple question for they.

questions.questionText: Why ___ Minh leave the office early yesterday?
questions.explanation: A past wh-question uses did before the subject and the base verb leave.

questions.questionText: I ___ my wallet at home, so I returned to get it.
questions.explanation: The meaning is that the speaker did not forget the wallet; use didn't plus forget.

questions.questionText: Did the children ___ the new game after school?
questions.explanation: The main verb stays in its base form after did.

questions.questionText: Which question has the correct word order?
questions.explanation: Place the wh-word first, then did, subject, and the base verb.

questions.questionText: She ___ the email yesterday, but she replied this morning.
questions.explanation: Use didn't plus the base verb read for the negative past event.

lessons.title: Integrated Past Events and Questions
lessons.objective: Combine regular and irregular past forms with affirmative, negative, and question structures in short narratives.
lessons.description: Select the correct past form and structure while following a sequence of completed events.
lessons.content: In a short account, use past simple for each completed event. Choose regular or irregular past forms in affirmative sentences. For negatives and questions, use did or didn't with the base verb. Finished-time expressions such as yesterday, last week, and two days ago help establish the time.
examples: We took the early train, visited the old town, and returned before dark.
commonErrors: Do not mix did with a past-form main verb: Did she see it?
Keep the event sequence in past simple when all actions are completed.
lessons.guidedPractice: Read a short event sequence, identify the finished-time context, and check each verb form.
lessons.summary: Use past forms in affirmative events and did/didn't plus the base verb in questions and negatives.

questions.questionText: Last Friday, we ___ the train, ___ the city museum, and ___ home late.
questions.explanation: The sentence lists completed events: take/took, visit/visited, and come/came.

questions.questionText: A: ___ you ___ the invitation? B: Yes, I ___ it yesterday.
questions.explanation: Questions use Did plus the base verb; the affirmative answer uses received.

questions.questionText: They ___ the wrong road, so they ___ at the hotel after midnight.
questions.explanation: The negative uses didn't plus take; the completed result uses regular past arrived.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports a completed visit last month?
questions.correctAnswer: My cousins came to our house and stayed for two days.
questions.explanation: Came is the irregular past of come and stayed is the regular past of stay.

options.text: My cousins came to our house and stayed for two days.
My cousins comed to our house and stay for two days.
My cousins come to our house and stayed for two days.
My cousins came to our house and stays for two days.

questions.questionText: Where ___ Hoa ___ her new coat last winter?
questions.explanation: A past wh-question uses did plus the base verb buy.

questions.questionText: I ___ the message last night, so I ___ you this morning.
questions.explanation: Didn't takes the base verb see; the affirmative completed event uses called.
questions.knowledgePoint: negative and regular past in context

questions.questionText: A: What time ___ the meeting ___? B: It ___ at three yesterday.
questions.explanation: The question uses did plus begin; the answer uses its irregular past began.
questions.knowledgePoint: irregular past in questions and answers

questions.questionText: Choose the correct short account of the school trip.
questions.correctAnswer: We left early, took a bus, and saw the lake.
questions.explanation: Left, took, and saw are the past forms of leave, take, and see.

options.text: We left early, took a bus, and saw the lake.
We leaved early, taked a bus, and seed the lake.
We leave early, took a bus, and see the lake.
We left early, take a bus, and saw the lake.

questions.questionText: ___ your sister ___ the tickets online, or did she buy them at the station?
questions.explanation: The first question clause uses Did plus the base verb book.

questions.questionText: Which pair correctly completes the account? They ___ breakfast at home, but they ___ lunch near the station.
questions.explanation: Had and ate are the past forms of have and eat.
